To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structural parameters of K 2 Ni F 4 -type perovskite-structured oxides are correlated with the oxygen nonstoichiometries, which is a result of interstitial oxygen formation.
the phase transition temperature of the Nd 2 Ni 4 +  δ decreases as P ( O 2 ) decreases.

the phase transition temperature and the lattice parameter of the layered perovskites decrease with increasing oxygen partial pressure and oxygen content, respectively, and that the lattice parameter perpendicular and parallel to the rock salt layer increases and decreases, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural changes in K 2 NiFe 4 -type perovskites, Nd 2 − x Sr x Ni 1 − x Cu x O 4 + δ.
the structural changes of the layered perovskites Nd 2 +  x Sr x  −  x NiO 3.5 +  δ in the course of thermal or chemical treatments.
the structural changes in the oxygen nonstoichiometries of K 2 Ni F 4 -type perovskite oxides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oxygen nonstoichiometries of Ni-based layered perovskites are determined by the competition between the oxygen vacancy and the interstitial oxygen.
the structural change in the K 2 NiFe 4 -type oxide is closely related to the oxygen nonstoichiometeric behavior.

the structural changes in Nd 2 +  x Sr x 2 NiO x 4 + δ are caused by the thermal expansion of oxygen octahedra and by the chemical expansion due to the formation of interstitial oxygen in the rock salt layers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oxygen nonstoichiometrical behavior of Ni-based layered perovskites is controlled by a competition between the oxygen intercalation and the oxygen ionization.
the interstitial-oxygen formation is strongly suppressed in K 2 NiFe 4 -type perovskite-related oxides.
the oxygen nonstoichiometrical behavior in K 2 NiFe 4 -type perovskites is governed not by the acceptor concentration but by the interstitial oxygen content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
structural information is very useful to make clear oxygen nonstoichiometrical behavior in K 2 NiFe 4 -type layered perovskites.
the oxygen nonstoichiometeries of the layered perovskites are controlled by the interstitial oxygen in the rock salt layers.
oxygen nonstoichiometries in Ni-based K  2 NiF 4 - and K  2 N i F 4 -related compounds are controlled by the acceptor concentration.
